questions.problem: A curve is defined as $y={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3x.$ Find the average rate of change of $y$ over the interval $[-1,3].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)={x}^{4}-3{x}^{3}+3x.$ Applying the formula for the average rate of change, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δy}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(3)-f(-1)}{3-(-1)} \\  & =\frac{[{3}^{4}-3({3}^{3})+3(3)]-[(-1)^{4}-3(-1)^{3}+3(-1)]}{4} \\  & =\frac{9-1}{4} \\  & =\frac{8}{4} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A curve is defined as $y=3x-5.$ Find the average rate of change of $y$ over the interval $[3,7].$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=3x-5.$ Applying the formula for the average rate of change, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δy}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(7)-f(3)}{7-3} \\  & =\frac{[3(7)-5]-[3(3)-5]]}{7-3} \\  & =\frac{16-4}{7-3} \\  & =\frac{12}{4} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}

questions.problem:
The table below lists values of $f(x)$ at distinct $x$-values. Knowing that the average rate of change of the function $f(x)$ on the interval $[2p,2]$ is $3,$ find the value of $p.$ 

| $x$ | $\,-9\,$ | $\,-4\,$ | $\,2p\,$ | $\,-1\,$ | $\,0\,$ | $\,1\,$ | $\,2\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\,-12\,$ | $\,-8\,$ | $\,-4\,$ | $\,-3\,$ | $\,2\,$ | $\,6\,$ | $\,8\,$ |
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the average rate of change, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(2)-f(2p)}{2-2p} \\  & =\frac{8-(-4)}{2-2p} \\  & =\frac{12}{2-2p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we know that $\frac{Δf}{Δx}=3$ on the interval $[2p,2].$ Thus, 

$$
\frac{12}{2-2p}=3.
$$

Solving for $p,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{12}{2-2p} & =3 \\ 12 & =3\cdot (2-2p) \\ 12 & =6-6p \\ 12-6 & =-6p \\ 6 & =-6p \\ \frac{6}{-6} & =\frac{-6p}{-6} \\ -1 & =p.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that $p=-1.$

questions.problem: The ice level in the North Pole is decreasing due to global warming. The thickness of ice, measured in feet, in the North Pole, is represented by the expression $135+0.1x-0.02{x}^{2},$ where $x$ is the time, in years, since measurements began. What is the average rate of decrease of the ice thickness over the first $10$ years?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=135+0.1x-0.02{x}^{2}$ be the thickness of the ice, in feet, after $x$ years. To find the average rate of change of the ice thickness over the first $10$ years, we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[0,10]$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(10)-f(0)}{10-0} \\  & =\frac{[135+0.1(10)-0.02(10)^{2}]-[135+0.1(0)-0.02(0)^{2}]}{10} \\  & =\frac{134-135}{10} \\  & =-0.1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of decrease of the ice thickness over the first $10$ years is $0.1$ feet per year.

questions.problem: The height $h(t),$ measured in feet, of a plant after $t$ years is given by the expression $h(t)=3{t}^{3/2}-2t.$ What is the average rate of growth over the first $4$ years?
questions.worked_solution:
Let $h(t)=3{t}^{3/2}-2t,$ the height measured in feet, of a plant after $t$ years. To find the average rate of change of $h(t)$ from $t=0$ to $t=4,$ we use the average rate of change formula on the interval $[0,4]:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δh}{Δt} & =\frac{h(b)-h(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{h(4)-h(0)}{4-0} \\  & =\frac{[3({4}^{3/2})-2(4)]-[3({0}^{3/2})-2(0)]}{4} \\  & =\frac{24-8}{4} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of growth is $4$ feet per year.

Example: 
                    Calculating the Average Rate of Change: Word Problem
canonical_examples.problem: Dave plants a tree in his garden. After $x$ months the tree is $2\sqrt x + 1$ feet high. What is the average rate of growth of the tree over the first six months?
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}+1$ be the height of the tree after $x$ months. The average rate of growth of the tree over the first six months is the average value of $f(x)$ on the interval $[0,6].$

Applying the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{f(6)-f(0)}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{6}+1-(2\sqrt{0}+1)}{6} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{6}}{6} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the average rate of growth is $\dfrac {\sqrt 6} 3 \approx 0.82$ feet per month.

This means we have to find an interval $[a,b]$ such that $f(a)=f(b).$ 

Since $f(-2)=f(5)=2,$ we conclude that $\dfrac{\Delta f}{\Delta x}=0$ on the interval $[-2,5].$
